detailed_rows.precise_target: For a bipartite H with bipartition A union B in which every vertex of A has degree at most r, there is C = C_H with ex(n,H) <= C n^{2-1/r} for all n.
detailed_rows.author_material: Complete printed proof with embedding schematic and closing square: C chosen from |A|+|B|, the displayed inequality n(2Cn^{-1/r})^r - binom(n,r)((|A|+|B|)/n)^r >= |B| resolved by taking C large, then dependent random choice at t=r to place the B-vertices, then the A-vertices one at a time against the at-most-r-neighbour bound and the >|A|+|B| common-neighbour supply.
detailed_rows.reason: Judged on this key's own load-bearing steps, not on the fact that a proof is printed and not on its sharing a mechanism with THEOREM:1.7.5. Step B (the dependent random choice invocation) is supplied by 1.7.5, and under the counting rules it is not counted twice; but that is a counting fact about one step, not a reason to grade the whole key as if it were 1.7.5. The key's own content is step A (calibrate the parameters so the extremal hypothesis alpha n^2/2 = C n^{2-1/r} and the printed display n(2Cn^{-1/r})^r - binom(n,r)((|A|+|B|)/n)^r >= |B| are jointly satisfiable with C depending only on |A|+|B|) and step C (embed the A-vertices one at a time, with m = |A|+|B| chosen so the exhaustion argument closes). Both are new here and locatable; both are also routine in kind - a substitution plus an elementary inequality, and the standard greedy-embedding pattern. Hence H1 on the substance of this key's own derivation. If either step were shown to be non-routine, this key would have to be graded on its own, and the count for the section would then be two units rather than one.
detailed_rows.shared_core_note: The dependent random choice construction is invoked here as a supplied same-package input at t=r; it is not treated as free background for grading 1.7.5 itself, and it is not counted a second time as this theorem's own core.
detailed_rows.if_1_7_5_is_settled_as_H2: Independent question. 1.7.5's level does not set this key's level in either direction; only this key's own added derivation and its own targeted comparison do.

core_steps.what: parameter choice: take C from |A|+|B| so that n(2Cn^{-1/r})^r - binom(n,r)((|A|+|B|)/n)^r >= |B|
core_steps.why_problem_specific: what has to be seen is that the threshold C may depend on |A|+|B| only, i.e. it is independent of n; the exponent 2-1/r then survives for fixed r. This step is not supplied by THEOREM:1.7.5.

core_steps.what: invoke the same-section dependent random choice at t=r, giving every r-subset of the embedded B-vertices more than |A|+|B| common neighbours
core_steps.why_problem_specific: this is THEOREM:1.7.5's construction; under the shared-core rule it is counted once and that count is taken at 1.7.5

core_steps.what: greedy one-at-a-time embedding of the A-vertices: at most r neighbours in B, and at most |A|+|B| vertices embedded so far, strictly fewer than the >|A|+|B| common-neighbour supply, so no required neighbourhood is exhausted
core_steps.why_problem_specific: the threshold |A|+|B| is chosen exactly so that this exhaustion argument closes; it is not |A|, not r, not r(|A|+|B|). The argument is problem-specific in its fit but standard in kind.
core_steps.classification: problem-specific greedy accounting, not a new construction

detailed_rows.distinctness: Not a duplicate of THEOREM:1.7.5 under the rules that compare hypotheses and conclusions: 1.7.1 assumes a fixed bipartite H with degree at most r on one side and concludes an extremal-number bound ex(n,H) <= C n^{2-1/r}; 1.7.5 assumes only a graph on n vertices with at least alpha n^2/2 edges and concludes the existence of a vertex set U whose r-subsets have more than m common neighbours. Different assumptions, different conclusions, different quantifiers over H. The two are therefore separate problems, and the level of one is not decided by the level of the other.
detailed_rows.own_added_derivation: What this key adds beyond invoking the same-section theorem is: (A) calibrate the parameters of 1.7.5 to the extremal setting - take t=r and alpha such that alpha n^2/2 equals Cn^{2-1/r}, i.e. alpha = 2C n^{-1/r}, then verify the printed inequality n(2Cn^{-1/r})^r - binom(n,r)((|A|+|B|)/n)^r >= |B| by taking C large depending only on |A|+|B| (equivalently (2C)^r - (|A|+|B|)^r/r! >= |B|); (C) run a greedy embedding of the A-vertices, where the choice m = |A|+|B| is what makes the exhaustion argument close: each A-vertex needs at most r B-neighbours, each has more than |A|+|B| common neighbours, and at most |A|+|B| vertices have been used so far.
detailed_rows.why_routine: Judged on that added derivation alone, not on the shared mechanism. (A) is a substitution plus an elementary inequality: one solves for alpha and checks a display, with no choice that a competent reader would have to invent rather than look for. (C) is the standard greedy-embedding pattern; the only insight is the size of the threshold, and once the supply is stated as |A|+|B| the observation 'more than the number used so far' is immediate. Neither is a construction of the kind counted elsewhere in this corpus as H2 (for example the Matthews checking-order construction with its 1/k last-state probability, or a marking rule with an invariant and coordinated update): here the object is supplied by another printed theorem and the work is calibration and a standard embedding. So the key is H1 on its own derivation being routine, and that conclusion does not rely on any claim that 1.7.1 and 1.7.5 must count as one.
detailed_rows.dedup_required_if_this_key_is_ever_upgra: Extend the existing targeted record with any new neighbour that becomes relevant; do not reuse 1.7.5's comparison as if the two statements were the same.

detailed_rows.precise_target: For positive integers n,r,m,t and alpha>0, every graph on n vertices with at least alpha n^2/2 edges has a U with |U| >= n alpha^t - binom(n,r)(m/n)^t such that every r-element subset of U has more than m common neighbours.
detailed_rows.author_material: Complete printed proof: with-replacement i.i.d. hosts u_1..u_t; random common neighbourhood A; E|A| = sum_v (deg(v)/n)^t >= n((1/n) sum_v deg(v)/n)^t >= n alpha^t by linearity and convexity with the average-degree bound; fixed-R probability ((# common neighbours of R)/n)^t; bad = at most m common neighbours so P(R subset A) <= (m/n)^t; sum over binom(n,r) subsets; delete one element per bad subset to get U with E|U| >= n alpha^t - binom(n,r)(m/n)^t, hence a U exists.
detailed_rows.reason: Judged on what the derivation actually carries, not on the proof being printed. The load-bearing steps are: (i) sample t hosts uniformly and independently WITH REPLACEMENT and take their common neighbourhood A - the induced correlation between the host set and A is the design decision that makes the method work, and r=1 exposes why an unconditioned vertex choice fails; (ii) convert the average-degree hypothesis into E|A| = sum_v (deg(v)/n)^t >= n((1/n) sum_v deg(v)/n)^t >= n alpha^t, where the convexity step is applied in the non-obvious direction to turn an average of powers into a power of an average; (iii) for fixed R compute P(R subset A) = (|N(R)|/n)^t and sum over the binom(n,r) bad r-subsets, which requires separating the random A from the fixed test set R; (iv) alter by deleting one vertex per bad r-subset, which destroys every bad subset at a cost bounded by the expected number of such subsets. Steps (i), (iii) and (iv) are specific to this construction rather than generic probabilistic-method background: the unit supplies a concrete, problem-specific mechanism whose design the reader could not read off any standard toolkit statement. That meets the H2 bar as applied elsewhere in this corpus (a printed author construction counted when the construction itself, not its verification, is the non-routine content). It is not H3: the construction is canonical in the field, the section presents it as the introduction of a known technique, and no research-level combination is required.
detailed_rows.shared_core_note: SUPERSEDES the earlier note 'If settled as H2 this is the section's single core; THEOREM:1.7.1 and the two exercises still do not count separately.' Step B of 1.7.1 - the invocation of this theorem's construction - is counted once and that count is taken here; that is a statement about one shared proof step, not about the identity of the two propositions. 1.7.1 is graded on its own added steps A and C (see its row) and is not folded into this key. The three exercises carry no author proof and are material_insufficient, which is a separate disposition and not a counting decision.

That inverts the project standard: difficulty is taken from the concrete non-routine core the author's proof actually carries, and print-completeness is not a downgrade basis. Symmetrically, a missing printed answer is not an upgrade basis.
rubric_correction.what_replaces_it: Each key is now handled by what its own material supports. THEOREM:1.7.5's load-bearing derivation is written out and decided H2. The three exercises have no printed author proof, so they are recorded as material_insufficient with difficulty unassessed - neither H1 nor H2.
